title: T. Rex Footprints Show How Fast It Walked
summary: Four fossil footprints are helping scientists learn about a dinosaur. They are the first known set of tracks likely left by an adult Tyrannosaurus rex. A trackway is three or more footprints in a row. This one is 7 meters long. The space between the prints shows the giant walked at about 1.6 meters per second. That is a quick walking pace for us. 'Finding an adult trackway is cool,' says Peter Falkingham, a scientist who studies fossils. The tracks were found by Kent Hups, a high school teacher. He found them in North Dakota last year. The first print was huge: 80 centimeters across, with three toes. The tracks are about 66.5 million years old. Scientists used the length of the steps and the size of the body to guess the speed. The prints are worn, so the speed is a guess. A fifth step may be hidden in the hill. The team waits for nature to wear away the rock. 'I can't wait to get back out there and keep looking for more,' Hups says.
why_it_matters: Dinosaur footprints are like clues from a crime scene, and learning to read them shows how scientists turn small clues into big discoveries.
